chapters.heading: UNITED STATES CAPITOL POLICE REFORM AND ACCOUNTABILITY

sections.heading: Definitions
paragraphs: (a) For the purposes of this act:

(i) The term “Capitol Police” means the United States Capitol Police. (ii) The term “Board” means the Capitol Police Board. (iii) The term “Chief” means the Chief of the United States Capitol Police. (iv) The term “United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds” means the United States Capitol, the Hall of the House of Representatives, the Senate Chamber, congressional offices, committee rooms, hearing rooms, galleries, cloakrooms, corridors, entrances, exits, ceremonial rooms, exterior grounds, and any building, room, facility, or area under the control of Congress, either House of Congress, an officer of either House, or the Capitol Police Board.

(v) The term “House-controlled area” means any chamber, room, office, committee room, gallery, hallway, entrance, facility, or other area under the control of the House of Representatives, the Speaker of the House, the House Sergeant at Arms, or any officer of the House. (vi) The term “Senate-controlled area” means any chamber, room, office, committee room, gallery, hallway, entrance, facility, or other area under the control of the Senate, the President pro tempore of the Senate, the Senate Sergeant at Arms, or any officer of the Senate. (vii) The term “shared congressional area” means any area of the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds not exclusively controlled by the House of Representatives or the Senate. (viii) The term “Member of Congress” means a Representative, Senator, Delegate, Resident Commissioner, or any person recognized as a Member under the rules of either House. (ix) The term “officer of Congress” means the Sergeant at Arms of either House, the Clerk of the House, the Secretary of the Senate, the Parliamentarian of either House, and the Chaplain of either House.

(x) The term “congressional proceeding” means a session, sitting, hearing, meeting, joint session, committee proceeding, conference, investigation, vote, debate, ceremony, or other official proceeding of either House of Congress or any committee thereof. (xi) The term “protective services” means security, escort, transportation, threat assessment, site protection, emergency response, access control, or other protection provided to a Member of Congress, officer of Congress, congressional employee, witness, invited guest, or other person lawfully connected to official congressional business.

chapter_notes.heading: Short Title
chapter_notes.text: (a) This Act may be cited as the “United States Capitol Police Reform and Accountability Act.”

chapter_notes.heading: Repeals and Supersession
chapter_notes.text: (a) The Uniformed Capitol Police Act of 2023 is hereby repealed. (b) The United States Capitol Police Technical Corrections Act is hereby repealed. (c) Any amendment, revision, technical correction, conforming change, authority, procedure, definition, office, power, duty, jurisdictional rule, or enforcement mechanism created by, made under, or dependent upon either Act repealed by this section is repealed and shall have no further force or effect. (d) Any law, rule, regulation, policy, directive, order, procedure, practice, or continuing authority inconsistent with this Act is superseded to the extent of the inconsistency. (e) Nothing in this section shall invalidate any lawful arrest, removal, protection, investigation, security measure, completed proceeding, or completed action taken before the effective date of this Act, except that no continuing authority may be claimed under any Act repealed by this section after this Act takes effect.

chapter_notes.heading: Severability
chapter_notes.text: (a) If any provision of this Act, or the application of any provision of this Act to any person, office, agency, circumstance, proceeding, area, or action, is held invalid, the remainder of this Act and the application of the remaining provisions to any other person, office, agency, circumstance, proceeding, area, or action shall not be affected. (b) If any authority granted under this Act is held invalid in part, such authority shall remain valid to the maximum extent permitted by law. (c) If any penalty, procedure, regulation, appointment, designation, reporting requirement, access rule, emergency authority, protective service, or enforcement power under this Act is held invalid in part, the remaining valid portion shall continue in effect unless the court or lawful authority determines that such portion cannot operate independently. (d) The repeal of any prior Act under this Act shall remain effective notwithstanding the invalidity of any separate provision of this Act, unless the provision held invalid is necessary to give effect to the repeal.

chapter_notes.heading: Rule of Construction
chapter_notes.text: (a) Nothing in this Act shall be construed to establish the Capitol Police as an executive department or agency. (b) Nothing in this Act shall be construed to place the Capitol Police under the direction, command, supervision, or control of the President or any executive department or agency, except to the extent expressly required by an Act of Congress or lawful court order. (c) Nothing in this Act shall be construed to prevent the executive branch from enforcing federal law, prosecuting offenses, executing warrants or court orders, protecting persons lawfully under executive protection, responding to emergencies, or providing lawful assistance to the Capitol Police. (d) Nothing in this Act shall be construed to authorize the Capitol Police to exercise general law-enforcement authority unrelated to Congress, congressional security, congressional proceedings, the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds, protected persons, official congressional business, temporary jurisdiction, emergency assistance, or another lawful basis expressly provided by this Act. (e) Nothing in this Act shall be construed to diminish the constitutional authority of either House of Congress over its own proceedings, chamber, rules, officers, privileges, discipline, controlled spaces, or internal security. (f) Nothing in this Act shall be construed to protect a Member of Congress from arrest, detention, removal, discipline, investigation, or prosecution for non-legislative criminal conduct, assault, threats, violence, weapons offenses, bribery, destruction of property, or any other conduct not itself protected by the Constitution, the rules of either House, or the lawful privileges of Congress. (g) Mothing in this Act shall be construed to authorize any officer, employee, agency, department, board, official, or person to use the Capitol Police for a political, retaliatory, partisan, personal, or viewpoint-discriminatory purpose.

chapter_notes.heading: Effective Date and Transition
chapter_notes.text: (a) This Act shall take effect immediately upon enactment. (b) Upon the effective date of this Act, the Uniformed Capitol Police Act of 2023, the United States Capitol Police Technical Corrections Act, and any continuing authority dependent upon either Act shall cease to have force or effect, except as otherwise preserved by this Act. (c) The United States Capitol Police, the Capitol Police Board, the Chief, the Deputy Chief, officers, employees, regulations, records, investigations, protective services, emergency measures, and other ongoing operations existing on the effective date of this Act shall continue under this Act to the extent consistent with this Act. (d) Any officer or employee of the Capitol Police lawfully serving before the effective date of this Act may continue to serve without reappointment, except where removal, reclassification, recommissioning, retraining, or other action is required by the Chief, the Board, this Act, or lawful regulation. (e) Any regulation, order, directive, access rule, emergency procedure, use-of-force policy, disciplinary rule, protective assignment, interagency arrangement, or other policy in effect before the effective date of this Act may remain in effect temporarily if consistent with this Act. (f) The Chief shall review existing regulations, orders, directives, access rules, emergency procedures, use-of-force policies, disciplinary rules, protective assignments, interagency arrangements, and other policies of the Capitol Police and shall revise, repeal, or reissue such policies as necessary to conform to this Act. (g) Any policy, order, regulation, procedure, appointment, designation, or authority inconsistent with this Act shall be superseded to the extent of the inconsistency. (h) Any investigation, complaint, disciplinary matter, arrest record, protective assignment, emergency action, or other pending matter existing on the effective date of this Act may continue under this Act, except that all further action shall comply with this Act. (i) The Board may issue temporary transition directives necessary to implement this Act, preserve the continuity of Capitol Police operations, maintain congressional security, and prevent disruption to the protection of the United States Capitol Buildings and Grounds. (j) Temporary transition directives issued by the Board shall remain in effect only until replaced by regulation, superseded by this Act, or repealed by the Board. (k) The Chief shall submit to the Board, within fourteen days after the effective date of this Act, a transition report identifying existing policies, regulations, personnel structures, interagency agreements, protective assignments, access rules, emergency procedures, and operational practices requiring revision under this Act. ○
